findings.reason: The protected SQL solution inner joins Warehouse and Products on product_id, multiplies units * Width * Length * Height for each row, and sums by warehouse.name AS warehouse_name. The query is concise, optimal, and single-pass; no candidate is required.

Joining Products attaches single-unit dimensions to each inventory row. Multiplying units by Width * Length * Height calculates exact total volume for that inventory line item, and GROUP BY warehouse.name aggregates the sum per warehouse correctly.

Joining W inventory rows to Products and grouping by warehouse takes O(W log W) time with sorting, or expected O(W) time with hash joins/aggregation. Auxiliary space is O(W). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Outputs columns warehouse_name and volume, handles warehouses with multiple distinct products, and correctly multiplies all three dimensions by unit counts.

The approach accurately details attaching product dimensions, multiplying by units, grouping by warehouse, and relational complexity bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover precomputing unit volumes in a CTE, correlated subqueries, pre-grouping units, shared products, and unused products.
